name: Legal Accounting Automation & Systems Integration
desc: A private workflow tool that connects legal invoice production with accounting review and posting. The app adds a human-reviewed automation layer for expense classification, approval, and cleaner handoff into legal accounting systems.
impact: Built a human-reviewed automation layer between legal operations and accounting workflows, with structured review queues, approval steps, and Actionstep posting support.
problem: Legal accounting work often depends on information moving cleanly between production systems, review steps, and accounting workflows.
built: I built a private integration layer that organizes incoming financial activity, supports staff review, applies configurable automation, and prepares approved items for posting into Actionstep legal accounting.
result: The workflow reduced repetitive administrative work, improved consistency, and created a clearer handoff between legal operations and accounting while keeping users in control of final decisions.

name: False Creek Pure Dental
desc: A production dental clinic website and workflow integration project for False Creek Pure Dental in Vancouver. I supported the WordPress site and connected practice-management workflows around OpenDental so the public website and clinic operations worked together more smoothly.
impact: Supported a live business website, WordPress maintenance, OpenDental workflow integration, and patient-facing booking/contact paths.
problem: The clinic needed its public website, booking paths, and practice-management workflows to feel connected instead of living as separate operational pieces.
built: I worked on the WordPress website and supported integration points around OpenDental workflows, helping bridge patient-facing web content with clinic administration needs.
result: The work made the site a more practical business tool: easier for patients to understand services and take action, and easier for the clinic to support day-to-day digital workflows.

name: Rate Your Landlord
desc: A full-stack tenant review platform that helps renters make more informed housing decisions. I built listing, review, rating, image upload, and map-based discovery flows, with the front end hosted on Netlify and the back end deployed on an Ubuntu server.
impact: Designed CRUD workflows, review submission, media upload, and deployment infrastructure.
problem: Renters often have very little information about the people and companies they rent from before signing a lease.
built: I built a searchable review platform with landlord listings, ratings, review creation, listing management, image uploads, and map-based discovery.
result: The app turns scattered tenant experiences into a more useful decision-making tool and gave me end-to-end practice across UI, API, file upload, deployment, and server operations.

name: Virtual Piano App
desc: An interactive browser piano for quick daily practice and music experiments. The app turns keyboard input and on-screen controls into playable notes, making it easy to explore React-driven audio interactions.
impact: Built a playable music interface and experimented with browser-based audio feedback.
problem: Practicing or experimenting with piano ideas is not always convenient when a real instrument is not nearby.
built: I created a browser-based piano that maps user input to playable notes and uses React state to keep the interface responsive.
result: The project helped me explore interactive audio, input handling, and playful front-end feedback in a focused, approachable app.

name: MusicAdventures
desc: A responsive musician website with event and conversation features. It was built to practice polished layouts, reusable styling, and API-backed content while keeping the experience simple for visitors.
impact: Created responsive pages, reusable components, and API-connected content sections.
problem: A band or music organization needs a simple public site that makes shows, media, and visitor conversation easy to browse.
built: I built responsive pages with reusable Sass patterns and connected the site to a provided API for dynamic content.
result: The finished site demonstrates clean layout structure, API consumption, responsive behavior, and front-end organization.

name: GDG DevFest 2022
desc: An event site for GDG Vancouver DevFest that connected to the Sessionize API to present schedule information clearly for attendees and volunteers.
impact: Integrated event data, improved schedule visibility, and supported the volunteer team.
problem: Event attendees and volunteers needed a clear way to browse DevFest sessions without digging through raw schedule data.
built: I helped build a React event experience that pulled session data from Sessionize and presented the schedule in a visitor-friendly format.
result: The site made event information easier to scan and gave the volunteer team a more useful public-facing schedule experience.
